images.seen: Two golfers with their bags on the fairway, watching a lightning strike come down the course, trees whipping in the wind. Wednesday.
lines: The eighteenth can wait; the sky is playing through.
That is the course's way of saying the round is over.
Two club selections left: the clubhouse or the car.

images.seen: An empty rugby stadium under an enormous black storm cloud, lightning behind the stands, floodlights on, pitch shining wet. Saturday.
lines: Kickoff is under review by the only official that outranks the referee.
The floodlights are on; the sky brought its own anyway.
The pitch is ready, the lines are marked, and the weather has the whistle.

images.seen: Storm aftermath on a bushveld lawn — wicker chairs flipped, cushions scattered, a lounger on its side, branches down, trees still bending under a dark sky. Tuesday.
lines: The storm rearranged the stoep furniture and did not ask anybody first.
The chairs are down, the branches are down, and the sky is not done.
Every loose object in the garden has chosen violence.

images.seen: An old farmer at the door of his rusted corrugated shed, hand on his hat, watching a massive black storm and dust wall roll across the dry veld. Sunday.
lines: He has seen fifty of these arrive, and he still comes out to watch.
Dust first, rain second: the order of business is written on the horizon.
The drought and the storm are about to have a word, and he wants to hear it.
